## Resolved

### F-082 — A substring audit of test titles breaks when prettier wraps the call

> _2026-09-15 · core/semantic-log · resolved_

The §5.1 parity audit in `core/semantic-log/test/parity.test.ts` proves that a named test exists by
searching the source for `t.test('<title>'`. One title ('a predecessor is not drained by fatal, …')
is long enough that prettier moved it onto the line after `t.test(`, so the audit failed even though
the test was present.

The lesson generalises: never resolve a name against raw source text — allow for formatting. The fix
matches with `t\.test\(\s*'<escaped title>'`, because the title itself is a string literal and is
never wrapped, so only the gap after the paren needs widening. Verified both ways: the real file
passes, and a copy with the title mutated fails exactly the two rows that reference it.

### F-153 — The editor's error view is not the gate; `ci-lint`'s `tsc` is

> _2026-09-14 · core/semantic-log · resolved_

An inline object spread (`{...maybeUndefined, leg}`) type-checked clean in the editor and in
`get_errors`, but `node --run ci-lint`'s `tsc` rejected it with TS2322, because the spread produces
an optional-property object. A clean editor at the moment of the edit means nothing; the gate is the
authority.

The fix was to make the merge total in a small helper rather than to cast. The obvious total form
(`leg === undefined || flow === undefined ? flow : merged`) buys a branch whose outcome is
unreachable by construction, which the 100% coverage gate would then flag, so the guard is written
with the short-circuit order that hides the impossible combination
(`if (flow === undefined || leg === undefined)`).

### F-154 — A test regex read off the rendered format was wrong by one character

> _2026-09-14 · core/semantic-log · resolved_

A test regex written from the rendered format said `flow=<id>/#-1` where the real token is
`flow=<id>/-#-1`: the empty-step placeholder is `-`, so the token reads `-#-1`. Read the failure
diff before touching the source — the source was right.

### F-155 — The unit tests were green while the end-to-end flow shape was wrong

> _2026-09-14 · core/semantic-log · resolved_

Rendering the flow artifact from a real run immediately showed two defects the fixtures could not:
`payer.discovery.parties` counted twice, because the declared-pair flags were re-created by each
declaring record so a chatty call site counted as two calls, and a missing `hub.transfer.deliver`
edge, because the closed-execution rule refused records that were emitted before the terminal one
but delivered after it. Both were invisible to fixtures that feed the ledger grouped per
participant.

For anything that reads arrival from several processes, the honest test drives the real processes.

### F-156 — `setWriter(null)` reads like silence but silences the whole process

> _2026-09-14 · core/semantic-log · resolved_

`setWriter(null)` looks like 'silence stdout' and is in fact the process-wide silence sentinel,
which silences a participant's service sink too (`logger.ts`). The artifact generator installed a
discarding primary writer instead. A helper whose name reads as 'do nothing' can do a great deal.

### F-159 — A failing test can be the finding, not a defect in the code

> _2026-09-14 · core/semantic-log · resolved_

The debounce test asserted that nothing is written inside the window, and it failed: `/events`
already writes the snapshot before it acknowledges a batch, so the window the test was probing never
existed. The premise was wrong, which is exactly why the debounce should not have existed — the
failing test was the finding, not a bug in the code under test.

Before 'fixing' a red test, read what the failure says about the assumption behind it.
